summary_paragraph: A woman with end-stage renal disease on hemodialysis and a history of prior cardiac surgery presented with severe chest pain and dyspnea. Evaluation revealed severe aortic stenosis due to deterioration of her bioprosthetic valve, along with non-intervenable coronary graft disease. She developed cardiogenic shock and acute respiratory failure, requiring intubation and vasopressor support. She underwent a redo sternotomy and mechanical aortic valve replacement. Postoperatively, she had transient atrial fibrillation, supratherapeutic INR managed with FFP, and a small pneumothorax. Her left arm AV fistula thrombosed and required revision after failed thrombectomy. She was successfully weaned from mechanical ventilation, transitioned to intermittent dialysis, and stabilized on warfarin and amiodarone. She was discharged to an extended care facility in stable condition on postoperative day 12 with plans for ongoing cardiac and dialysis follow-up.
